captions.detailed: A 3D-printable flexible helical shaft coupling. It consists of a solid cylindrical body with a central helical cut that provides flexibility, flanked by two solid cylindrical end collars. Each collar features a central axial bore for shaft insertion and two perpendicular through-holes for set screws.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric helical shaft coupling in OpenSCAD that connects two shafts of different diameters. The model should include customizable parameters for the coupling's outer diameter, upper and lower shaft bore diameters, individual end collar lengths, helical section length, and set-screw hole diameters.
captions.factory: The design is built using three primary sections translated along the Z-axis. The top and bottom collars are generated using a custom 'rod_connector' module which subtracts an inner shaft cylinder and two orthogonal set-screw cylinders from a main outer cylinder. The central flexible helix is created using 'linear_extrude' with a 720-degree twist, extruding a 2D profile formed by subtracting a smaller circle and a half-space square from a larger circle.
